spec.name: Crossover 25/223
spec.notes: Trend crossover: short mean of returns against a long one.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.1, annual return 4%, maximum drawdown 11%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.09 to 1.07 (change -0.02).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.09 to 1.09. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 0.93 (as submitted, 5 bps: 1.09); it breaks even at 39.8 bps with daily turnover 0.05.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.09 against 1.09 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -0.31 against 1.09 in research, a gap of +1.40.
The best year gives 29% of total P&L (year 5) and calm regimes give -32%; Sharpe is -0.26 in calm and 4.27 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 78 distinct specs; the best of 78 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 1.16, so the claimed 1.10 becomes -0.06 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 43%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.24 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.60).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.09 to as low as 0.17 (as low as 0.50 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (21 days) give 72% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 38% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
